Issued at 300 AM EDT Sun Aug 23 2026

Today-Tonight...A deep mid-level trough is forecast to remain 
situated across the eastern US, with a shortwave rounding the 
trough and moving across the Florida peninsula today. At the 
surface, east central Florida remains sandwiched between the 
Atlantic ridge axis to the south and a quasi-stationary boundary 
draped across the southeastern US to the north. A plume of 
moisture will work across central Florida today, with the 
shortwave aloft assisting with shower and storm development along 
with the typical diurnal pattern. Isolated to scattered showers 
and storms will start late this morning near and north of the I-4 
corridor, with coverage expanding southward through the afternoon 
hours. Activity will then shift eastward towards the coast, where 
additional interactions with the east coast sea breeze may support
further development of activity. The highest rain and storm 
chances (50-60%) are focused near and north of the I-4 corridor 
where moisture is anticipated to be greatest today. While some hi-
res guidance continues to favor this evolution of activity, it is 
important to note that drier air aloft could act as a limiting 
factor for shower and storm development. Decided to lean slightly 
more towards an active pattern given the mid-level support and 
plume of moisture present, hence the slight discrepancy in the 
forecast when compared to the NBM. The environment continues to 
look favorable for storm development, with diurnal heating 
increasing instability, dry air aloft supporting downbursts, and 
the plume of moisture supporting heavy rainfall. Hazards today 
will include frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts of 45-55 mph, 
and quick rainfall accumulations of 1-3". Westerly steering flow 
will keep activity moving offshore, with a gradual decline in 
coverage into the evening and overnight hours. Activity may even 
diminish slightly quicker than forecast given the earlier 
potential start time, and adjustments to the forecast will be made
as needed depending on how things evolve today. Additional shower
and storm development across the local Atlantic waters cannot be 
ruled out overnight, especially across the Gulf Stream waters.

Outside of showers and storms, anticipate higher cloud coverage 
which will help keep temperatures closer to normal values today. 
Highs reach the low 90s, combining with humidity to produce peak 
heat indices of 102F to 107F. The greatest peak heat indices are 
anticipated across the Treasure Coast, where cloud coverage may 
not be quite as high. Residents and visitors are strongly 
encouraged to practice heat safety to avoid developing heat 
illness. Overnight, temperatures fall into the mid 70s.

Monday-Tuesday...The deep troughing across the eastern US begins 
to lift northeastward and weaken, resulting in the weakening of 
the surface boundary draped across the southeast US. The surface 
Atlantic high is forecast to lift northward in response, with the 
ridge axis draping across the Florida peninsula. Locally, this 
will result in light southerly flow both Monday and Tuesday, 
allowing for both easier development and intrusion inland of the 
east coast sea breeze. Drier air is forecast to filter across the 
area on Monday, with the southerly flow slowly advecting moisture 
back towards east central Florida into Tuesday. This drier air 
will result in below- normal rain chances, ranging between 20-30% 
on Monday and 20-40% on Tuesday. Any activity that does manage to 
develop will be favored in the afternoon hours, driven primarily 
by the sea breezes and any subsequent interactions. Storm hazards 
will include frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts 45-55 mph, and
heavy downpours. Lighter steering flow aloft both Monday and 
Tuesday may lead to slow and erratic storm motions, which will 
also increase the potential for minor, localized flooding in some 
spots if showers and storms do manage to develop. Overall, weak 
southwesterly flow aloft will support movement towards the east 
coast, with activity pushing offshore through the late evening and
overnight hours. Continued development across the local Atlantic 
waters will be possible each night, with mostly dry conditions 
across the peninsula. Temperatures are forecast to remain near to 
slightly above normal each afternoon, with highs near and north of
the I-4 corridor reaching the mid 90s, with highs in the low 90s 
elsewhere. At this time, peak heat indices are forecast to range 
between 102F to 107F, remaining just below Heat Advisory criteria.
Those spending extended periods of time outdoors will need to 
remain adequately hydrated and take breaks in the shade or A/C to 
prevent the development of heat-related illness. Overnight, 
temperatures are anticipated to remain near normal in the mid 70s.
